q: The Bt protoxin produced by Bacillus thuringiensis is converted to its active toxin form under which condition?
High temperature inside the plant cell
Alkaline pH of the insect gut
Acidic pH of the insect foregut
UV exposure on the leaf surface
The inactive protoxin is converted into the activated toxin form specifically under the alkaline pH conditions found in the gut of susceptible insects.
Which cry gene product specifically controls the corn borer?
cryIAb controls the corn borer, while cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms.
Golden Rice is a genetically modified crop developed mainly to address deficiency of which vitamin?
Golden Rice was engineered to be enriched in Vitamin A, addressing a common nutritional deficiency.
In nature, RNAi acts as a cellular defence mechanism primarily against:
RNAi exists naturally in eukaryotic cells as a defence against RNA viruses and transposons ('jumping genes').
Which vector is used to introduce nematode-specific genes into a host plant for RNAi-based resistance?
Agrobacterium is used as the vector to deliver nematode-specific DNA into the host plant genome.
Which plant part is protected from nematode infestation using RNAi in tobacco?
The RNAi technique is used to prevent infestation of tobacco plant roots by the nematode Meloidegyne incognitia.
The first-ever clinical gene therapy, given in 1990, was used to treat:
The first clinical gene therapy was administered in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
In the gene therapy procedure for ADA deficiency, the functional ADA cDNA is introduced into the patient's lymphocytes using:
Direct microinjection into red blood cells
A retroviral vector is used to introduce the functional ADA cDNA into cultured lymphocytes isolated from the patient.
ELISA (Enzyme Linked Immuno Sorbent Assay) is based on the principle of:
ELISA works on the principle of antigen-antibody interaction, detecting either pathogen antigens or the antibodies raised against them.
PCR is used to detect mutations in genes of patients suspected of having which disease, as per the source notes?
PCR is used to detect mutations in genes of patients suspected of having cancer, in addition to detecting HIV in suspected AIDS patients.
What proportion of all transgenic animals produced to date are mice?
Although transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have been produced, over 95% of all transgenic animals are mice.
Rosie, the first transgenic cow produced in 1997, is notable because her milk contained:
A higher fat percentage than normal cow milk
Extra vitamin D for stronger bones
Rosie produced milk containing the human protein alpha-lactalbumin (2.4 g/litre), making it more nutritionally balanced for human babies.
Which human protein, used in treating emphysema, has been produced using transgenic animals?
Alpha-1-antitrypsin, used to treat emphysema, is a biological product manufactured using transgenic animals.
Transgenic mice are used to check the safety of which vaccine, as mentioned in the source notes?
Transgenic mice are used to test the safety of polio vaccines before they are used in humans.
In 1997, an American company obtained a US patent related to which crop variety, later disputed as being derived by Indian farmers?
The American company obtained patent rights on a 'new' Basmati rice variety, even though it was actually derived by Indian farmers crossing Indian Basmati with…
Which two traditional Indian medicinal resources, besides Basmati rice, have been subjects of patent disputes as per the source notes?
Neem and turmeric, both used for ages in traditional Indian medicine, have also been subjects of patent disputes.
Bacillus thuringiensis is best described as:
Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is a soil bacterium that produces insecticidal crystal proteins.
The name of the Bt toxin gene, cry, is short for:
The toxin gene is called cry, short for crystal, referring to the protein crystal it encodes.
Which two cry genes, when introduced into cotton, together control cotton bollworms?
cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms, while cryIAb controls the corn borer.
The specific target of the activated Bt toxin inside a susceptible insect is the:
The activated toxin binds to the epithelial cells of the insect midgut, creating pores.
Once pores are created in midgut epithelial cells by the activated Bt toxin, the immediate effect on those cells is that they:
Divide rapidly to repair the damage
Pore formation causes midgut epithelial cells to swell and lyse (burst), eventually killing the insect.
Golden Rice illustrates which specific category of GM crop benefit?
Golden Rice is the example given for enhanced nutritional value among the listed GM crop benefits.
Which molecule does the complementary RNA strand bind to in order to trigger silencing?
A complementary RNA strand binds to the target mRNA, forming a double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), which triggers silencing.
What is the fate of a target gene whose mRNA has been converted into dsRNA?
It is duplicated across the genome
It is exported to a neighbouring cell
Once the target mRNA forms dsRNA, it cannot be translated, so expression of the corresponding gene is blocked/silenced.
Besides RNA virus infection, what is another natural source of complementary RNA that can trigger RNAi in a eukaryotic cell?
The complementary RNA involved in natural RNAi may originate from infection by RNA viruses, or from transposons within the cell.
What does the abbreviation dsRNA stand for?
dsRNA stands for double-stranded RNA, formed when complementary RNA strands anneal.
What happens when sense and anti-sense RNA strands meet inside a transgenic host cell?
They anneal/bind to form double-stranded RNA
They fuse into a single protein
They are exported out of the plant
Being complementary, the sense and anti-sense RNA strands bind/anneal to each other, forming double-stranded RNA.
Which specific nematode species is targeted by the RNAi technique described for tobacco?
The RNAi technique described protects tobacco plant roots from the nematode Meloidegyne incognitia.
Complementary RNA in natural RNAi may arise from infection by which type of pathogen?
The complementary RNA involved in natural RNAi may originate from infection by RNA viruses, or from transposons.
In the transgenic tobacco RNAi system, which organism serves as the vector to deliver the nematode-specific gene?
Agrobacterium is used as the vector to introduce nematode-specific genes into the host plant.
As per the source notes, how many recombinant therapeutics are presently marketed in India?
About 30 recombinant therapeutics have been approved worldwide; of these, 12 are presently marketed in India.
Mature, functional human insulin is formed after which peptide chain is removed from the pro-hormone?
Pro-insulin has three chains, A, B and C; mature insulin has only chains A and B after the C-peptide is removed.
Which American company prepared human insulin by this recombinant method in 1983?
In 1983, the American company Eli Lilly prepared human insulin using the recombinant DNA method.
The first-ever clinical gene therapy in 1990 was given to a patient suffering from which condition?
The first-ever clinical gene therapy was given in 1990 to a 4-year-old girl with adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency.
ADA deficiency is a genetic disorder that primarily causes problems with which body system?
ADA deficiency is a genetic disorder in which the gene for the ADA enzyme is deleted or defective, causing problems with the immune system.
In the gene therapy procedure for ADA deficiency, which cells are isolated from the patient's blood and cultured in vitro?
Lymphocytes are isolated from the patient's blood and cultured in vitro as the first step of the gene therapy procedure.
A functional ADA cDNA is introduced into the patient's cultured lymphocytes using which type of vector?
A retroviral vector is used to introduce the functional ADA cDNA into the patient's cultured lymphocytes.
Rising demand for insulin worldwide is mainly linked to increasing cases of which condition?
Demand for insulin is rising due to increasing cases of adult-onset diabetes.
According to the source notes, PCR is used to detect gene mutations in patients suspected of having which disease?
PCR is used to detect mutations in genes of patients suspected of having cancer, in addition to detecting HIV in suspected AIDS patients.
ELISA is based on which underlying principle?
ELISA (Enzyme Linked Immuno Sorbent Assay) is based on the principle of antigen-antibody interaction.
In diagnosis by radioactive-probe hybridisation, what technique is used to detect the binding of the probe to the patient's gene?
After the probe hybridises with the patient's DNA/gene, autoradiography is used to detect the binding.
Which combination of technologies is highlighted in the source notes as together enabling early molecular diagnosis?
Recombinant DNA technology, PCR and ELISA
Recombinant DNA technologies, PCR and ELISA are highlighted as the key technologies enabling early molecular diagnosis of disease.
In the hybridisation-based diagnostic procedure, what is hybridised with the patient's DNA?
A second sample of the patient's own blood
A random fragment of bacterial plasmid
A sample of the patient's urine
A gene-specific radioactive probe is hybridised with the patient's DNA/gene, and autoradiography detects the binding.
Transgenic rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have all been produced, but which animal makes up over 95% of all existing transgenic animals?
Over 95% of all existing transgenic animals are mice, even though rats, rabbits, pigs, sheep, cows and fish have also been produced.
The human protein alpha-1-antitrypsin, produced using transgenic animals, is primarily used to treat which condition?
Alpha-1-antitrypsin, used to treat emphysema, is a biological product manufactured using transgenic animals.
Besides alpha-1-antitrypsin production, similar transgenic-animal approaches are being tried for producing treatments for which two conditions?
Similar transgenic-animal approaches for producing biological products are being tried for phenylketonuria (PKU) and cystic fibrosis.
Rosie, produced in 1997, is remembered in biotechnology history as the first transgenic:
Rosie, produced in 1997, was the first transgenic cow, and her milk contained the human protein alpha-lactalbumin.
Rosie's milk was considered more nutritionally balanced for human babies than natural cow milk because it was enriched in:
Rosie's milk was enriched in the human protein alpha-lactalbumin, making it more nutritionally balanced for human babies than natural cow milk.
Transgenic mice are used before human trials mainly to test the safety of which type of product?
Vaccines, such as the polio vaccine
Transgenic mice are used to test the safety of vaccines, such as the polio vaccine, before it is used on humans.
In 1997, which organisation granted patent rights on a 'new' Basmati rice variety to an American company?
The US Patent and Trademark Office
In 1997, an American company obtained patent rights on a 'new' Basmati rice variety from the US Patent and Trademark Office.
Besides Basmati rice, which two traditional Indian medicinal resources have also been subjects of patent disputes?
Neem and turmeric, both used for ages in traditional Indian medicine, have also been subjects of patent disputes.
Inadequate compensation given back to developing countries whose bio-resources were exploited is considered a matter of:
Inadequate compensation and benefit-sharing given back to poorer/developing countries whose resources were used is considered a matter of injustice.
In Bacillus thuringiensis, the toxin gene responsible for producing the insecticidal crystal protein is called:
The toxin is encoded by the cry (crystal) gene in the bacterium.
Bt cotton is resistant to which group of pests?
Bt cotton, carrying cryIAc and cryIIAb genes, is resistant to cotton bollworms.
The double-stranded RNA formed during RNA interference fails to bring about gene expression because it:
dsRNA formed by annealing of complementary RNA strands cannot be translated, silencing the corresponding gene.
RNAi technology has been used to make tobacco plants resistant to which organism?
RNAi is used to protect tobacco roots from the nematode Meloidegyne incognitia.
Which enzyme's deficiency causes the immune disorder treated in the world's first clinical gene therapy (1990)?
The 1990 gene therapy treated adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency, a genetic immune disorder.
Repeated infusions of genetically engineered lymphocytes are required in ADA gene therapy mainly because:
ADA cDNA cannot integrate into lymphocyte DNA
Lymphocytes are not immortal and eventually die
The patient's immune system rejects lymphocytes
The retroviral vector is degraded instantly
Since lymphocytes have a limited lifespan and are not immortal, the corrected cells eventually die, requiring periodic reinfusion of newly engineered lymphocytes.
PCR is used to detect the presence of which virus in suspected AIDS patients?
PCR is used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients by amplifying viral DNA sequences.
The first transgenic cow, Rosie, produced milk containing the human protein alpha-lactalbumin at a concentration of approximately:
Rosie's milk contained the human milk protein alpha-lactalbumin at about 2.4 grams per litre, making it more nutritionally balanced for human babies.
GEAC stands for Genetic Engineering Approval Committee, the Indian body that regulates and approves GM organisms/research.
Rosie's milk contained about 2.4 grams of human alpha-lactalbumin per litre. Approximately how much would be present in 5 litres of her milk?
2.4 grams/litre × 5 litres = 12 grams of alpha-lactalbumin in 5 litres of Rosie's milk.
Golden Rice is genetically engineered to be rich in which vitamin?
Golden Rice is a GM rice variety engineered to be rich in Vitamin A, illustrating enhanced nutritional value.
Which vector is used to introduce nematode-specific genes into tobacco for RNAi-based resistance?
Agrobacterium is used as the vector to introduce nematode-specific genes into the tobacco plant.
About how many recombinant therapeutics have been approved worldwide for human use, as per the source notes?
About 30 recombinant therapeutics have been approved worldwide for human use; 12 of these are presently marketed in India.
A permanent cure for ADA deficiency would require introducing the normal gene into cells at which stage?
A very early embryonic developmental stage
A permanent cure requires introducing the normal ADA gene into cells at a very early embryonic developmental stage, such as bone-marrow stem cells.
Rosie, the first transgenic cow, was produced in which year?
Rosie, the first transgenic cow, was produced in 1997 and produced milk enriched with the human protein alpha-lactalbumin.
Which body decides on the validity of GM-related research and its use for public utility in India?
GEAC (Genetic Engineering Approval Committee) decides on the validity of GM-related research and its use for public utility in India.
